text:
Maya (CS): FYI — getting multiple customer reports about degraded answer quality since the draft/speculative rollout last night. Patterns: missing steps in how-to answers, factual hallucinations, and truncated lists. Not everyone but several enterprise customers. Raising priority.
Lina (Support): Customer snippets attached. Customer "DataForge" says their QA tests that used to pass now return wrong SQL and sometimes "I don't know" for straightforward prompts. Repro steps from them below.
Lina (Support): Repro (from DataForge):

```
POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
Authorization: Bearer $KEY
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "model": "redwood-draft-1",
  "prompt": "Generate a SQL query to find active users in last 30 days with email domain 'example.com'",
  "max_tokens": 200,
  "temperature": 0.0,
  "speculative_decoding": true
}

Response (before rollout - expected):
{
  "text": "SELECT user_id, email FROM users WHERE last_active >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '30 days' AND email LIKE '%@example.com'"
}

Response (after rollout - observed):
{
  "text": "I can't be sure about the schema, but maybe check users table?"
}
```

Lina (Support): They ran 5x with same prompt and saw inconsistent outputs. They also tried model: "redwood-stable-1" and got the expected SQL.

Alex (ML): Thanks — this sounds like a decoding/ sampling change leaking into deterministic-regime requests. Do we have the rollout id? Which config toggles were flipped?

Maya (CS): Rollout metadata from release notes: rollout-id=release/2026-03-14/draft-sampling-v2, started 2026-03-14 02:12 UTC. It enabled the new speculative decoding path and adjusted prefix caching heuristics.

deploy-bot: deploy event: release/2026-03-14/draft-sampling-v2 promoted to hosted-prod in us-west1 @ 2026-03-14T02:12:39Z (link: https://deploys.redwood/release/2026-03-14/draft-sampling-v2)

John (SRE): No anomaly in infra metrics: p95 latency and GPU error rates look normal in the timeframe. So more likely model/decoder behavior than infra.

Alex (ML): Could be speculative decoding path increasing nondeterminism even at temperature=0.0 due to internal draft sampling heuristics. Need: 1) exact API request headers/payload from customer (incl. any experimental flags), 2) model binary/commit for that rollout, 3) a minimal repro harness we can run against the same model variant.

Lina (Support): I attached raw request logs from DataForge (sanitized keys). They set temperature=0.0 and top_p default, but speculative_decoding was implicitly enabled because they were auto-matched to redwood-draft-1. They also gave a failing customer prompt -> I pasted above.

Ravi (Product): Severity: DataForge is mid-enterprise on dedicated plan. They called in and are P1-ing this because it breaks test automation. We should consider immediate rollback if scope is > 1 customer. What's the blast radius?

Maya (CS): Other reports: "Ledgerly" saw similar missing steps in a finance checklist generator. "HelpdeskCo" saw hallucinated policy citations. So far 4 customers filed tickets in last 6 hours. No billing/auth errors — purely quality regression.

Alex (ML): Quick checks I'll run: reproduce prompt against the deployed draft variant and earlier stable variant, with deterministic seeds and with speculative_decoding toggled off. If disabling speculative fixes output, we can ship an emergency config change to disable that path while keeping rollout. Will also run n=10 replicates to measure variance.

Alex (ML): Repro command (internal):

```bash
# call hosted model variant directly (internal debug endpoint)
curl -s -X POST https://int-api.redwood/v1/debug/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $INT_KEY" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-draft-1","prompt":"Generate a SQL query to find active users in last 30 days with email domain 'example.com'","max_tokens":200,"temperature":0.0,"speculative_decoding":true,"seed":42}'
```

Alex (ML): If that returns bad outputs but the same call with "speculative_decoding": false returns good output, that's a smoking gun. I'll run now and post results.

John (SRE): If we need rollback, what's the easiest? Re-deploy prior config (release/2026-03-14/draft-sampling-v1) or flip feature flag? Which is faster?

Ravi (Product): Feature flag flip preferred if we can, to avoid full rollback of other unrelated changes. But need ML + infra to confirm the flag covers the speculative path.

Alex (ML): The speculative path is behind a runtime flag we can flip per-region. I'll prepare a safe rollback playbook: flip flag -> monitor 10 customers' smoke tests -> if pass, keep flag; else full rollback.

Maya (CS): Can we do a targeted mitigation for affected customers (DataForge) in the meantime? e.g., route them to redwood-stable-1 or force speculative=false in proxy?

Lina (Support): Yes we can override on their account token and force model=redwood-stable-1. I can do that if Product approves. They asked for minimal disruption.

Ravi (Product): Approve temporary per-customer override. Lina, please route DataForge and Ledgerly to stable variant as stopgap and let them know we're investigating.

Alex (ML): Update: initial repro shows that with speculative_decoding=true, temperature=0 still produced variable and lower-quality SQL. With speculative_decoding=false the outputs match pre-rollout expected answers across 20 runs. So it's reproducible.

Alex (ML): Hypothesis: the speculative path allows speculative token proposals from auxiliary sampler that occasionally collapse to fallback text like "I can't be sure" when prefix scoring thresholds differ. We'll collect token-level logs and compare decode trajectories.

John (SRE): To flip flag: I'll coordinate with infra. Need a CSR ticket id and owner. Also list of canary accounts to monitor and health checks.

Maya (CS): CSR ticket created: CS-13892. I'll add affected customers and attach sample logs. Owner: Maya (CS).

deploy-bot: feature-flag: "enable_speculative_decoding" toggled ON in rollout v2 @ 2026-03-14T02:12:39Z

Alex (ML): Proposed immediate actions:
1) ML: push a runtime config that disables speculative decoding at request-time (per-customer / per-region flag).
2) Support: route impacted customers to stable model variant and inform them of the temporary fix.
3) SRE: prepare flag rollback playbook and runbook for quick flip with monitoring.
4) Eng: gather token-level decode traces, model commit, and perf diffs.

Lina (Support): Doing the stable-route overrides now for DataForge + Ledgerly + HelpdeskCo. Will notify them with a note and ETA < 2h. :thumbsup:

John (SRE): I'll schedule a flag flip in us-west1 now. Monitoring hooks: errors, p95 latency, and run the customers' smoke prompts through the canary path every 5min for 30min.

Alex (ML): I'll upload the first batch of decode traces and a short analysis thread once I have token-level differences. If we confirm this is the root cause, we need to revert the speculative heuristics and run a regression suite against our customer prompt corpus before re-enabling.

Ravi (Product): Good. Post-mortem items: add pre-rollout regression tests for critical customers + extend canary size checks. Also need clearer telemetry for decoding-mode toggles.

Maya (CS): Thanks all. I'll keep this thread updated and escalate to SLA team if any customer remains unhappy after mitigation. Please ping if you need customer contact info or more logs.

Alex (ML): Quick note for debug: please include request-id headers from customer logs (x-request-id) so we can match traces across systems. Also include model commit hash if available.

Lina (Support): Got the request-ids and attached to CS-13892. Noted.

Maya (CS): Updating status: overrides applied, SRE flipping flag in us-west1 now. Will report back here once we confirm improvements.

John (SRE): Flag flipped at 2026-03-14T04:39:12Z in us-west1. Initial smoke shows DataForge example now returns expected SQL on 10/10 runs. Monitoring for the next 30m.

Maya (CS): DataForge confirmed initial tests passing. They still want root cause and timeline for re-enable.

Alex (ML): Saving a note: need follow-up to harden speculative decoding path, add deterministic fallback for low-temp requests, and expand pre-rollout evals. I'll open ML-issue 452 and link here.

Ravi (Product): Thanks team. Once ML-issue 452 has a proposed fix, we'll plan a canary with expanded safety checks before re-enabling.

Maya (CS): Closing loop: customer-facing mitigation done, internal ticketing in place. Will keep thread open until post-mortem is published.

Maya (CS): cc @Ravi (Product) @Alex (ML) @John (SRE) for visibility. :white_check_mark:
